name: application-theme-toggle-switch
title: Theme Toggle Switch
description: Three-way Light/Dark/System theme selector built as a real radio group with icons and a contrasting pill background on the selected option.
useWhen: Letting users choose between light, dark, and OS-matching ("system") appearance.
You want a segmented control rather than a binary switch, since "system" is a genuine third state, not just an intermediate value.
The choice needs icon + label pairing so the option is clear without relying on icon recognition alone.
avoidWhen: Your app only supports light and dark (no system/auto mode) — a binary switch from the Toggles primitive is simpler and clearer.
You need the control to live inside a menu item rather than as a standalone segmented control — compose a menu item with a smaller instance instead.
responsiveBehavior: The control is a fixed-width inline-flex group sized to its content; it doesn't reflow at different widths since its label set is always three short words.
accessibility: Built on real radio inputs grouped by a shared name, wrapped in a <fieldset>/<legend> (visually hidden) — so it behaves like a native radio group for keyboard and screen reader users, including arrow-key navigation between options.
The selected option's pill background is a secondary visual cue; the underlying checked radio state is always the source of truth.
Each option pairs an icon with visible text, so meaning never depends on icon recognition alone.

variants.title: Theme Toggle Switch
variants.description: A three-way Light/Dark/System control with Light selected (white pill background) against a gray track.
accessibility: Standard radio-group keyboard navigation (arrow keys move selection) works without any custom key handling.

variants.title: Theme Toggle Switch (Dark)
variants.description: The same three-way control adapted for dark surfaces, shown with Dark selected.
accessibility: Selected-pill contrast against the dark track remains distinguishable in both directions of the toggle.
